explanation:
In modern C++, 'enum class' introduces scoped enumerations that encapsulate enumerator names within a dedicated scope, preventing name collisions and improving type safety. Unlike traditional enums, enum classes do not implicitly convert to integers or other types, enforcing explicit conversions and reducing bugs. This feature enhances code clarity and maintainability by clearly associating enumerators with their enumeration type and avoiding polluting the global namespace.

In modern C++, scoped enums (declared with 'enum class') provide a type-safe and strongly scoped enumeration. Unlike traditional enums, they do not implicitly convert to integers, preventing accidental misuse and name pollution. Scoped enums improve code clarity and maintainability by encapsulating enumeration constants within a specific scope, which is especially useful in large codebases or when defining enumerations like seek directions in stream buffers.
